title: Benchmarking Pretrained Molecular Embedding Models For Molecular Representation Learning
abstract: arXiv:2508.06199v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Pretrained molecular embedding models spanning graph neural networks, text transformers, and hybrid architectures have been widely used in drug discovery, yet no large-scale, rigorous comparison of their representations existed. We evaluated 28 models across 25 classification datasets under a controlled framework using hierarchical Bayesian Bradley-Terry statistical testing. All neural models except CheMeleon failed to outperform the classical ECFP count fingerprint; CheMeleon was the only model rated as better. However, further testing on external validation datasets, based on scaffold cross-validation and a Bayesian hierarchical correlated t-test, revealed no definite advantage of either embedding method. As a practical takeaway, we recommend evaluating both ECFP fingerprints and CheMeleon embeddings in novel QSAR/QSPR studies. translated_title: 面向分子表示学习的预训练分子嵌入模型基准测试
translated_abstract: 覆盖图神经网络、文本Transformer和混合架构的预训练分子嵌入模型已被广泛应用于药物发现领域，然而此前尚缺乏对其表示能力的大规模严格比较。我们在一个受控框架下，采用层次贝叶斯Bradley-Terry统计检验方法，在25个分类数据集上对28个模型进行了评估。结果显示，除CheMeleon外，所有神经模型均未能超越经典的ECFP计数指纹，CheMeleon是唯一被评为优于ECFP指纹的模型。然而，基于支架交叉验证和贝叶斯层次相关t检验的外部验证数据集的进一步测试表明，两种嵌入方法均不具备明确的优势。作为实用的结论，我们建议在新的QSAR/QSPR研究中同时评估ECFP指纹和CheMeleon嵌入。总体而言，就所有被评估的神经网络而言，这些结果也挑战了人们所认为的（神经模型的优势）。
tldr: 本研究对28个预训练分子嵌入模型进行了大规模基准测试，发现除CheMeleon外所有神经模型均未超越经典ECFP计数指纹，且外部验证显示两者并无明确优劣，建议在新QSAR/QSPR研究中同时评估这两种方法。
